question: Which of the following metals was first used by man?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Copper**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Copper** was the first metal to be used by humans, marking the end of the Stone Age and the beginning of the Copper Age.
 
• It was used in the creation of tools and weapons, which were more durable than those made of stone.
 
• The use of copper dates back to around 10,000 years ago, with evidence of copper smelting found in archaeological sites.
 
• Copper is easily extracted and worked with, making it an ideal first metal for early human societies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Magnesium**

 
 
• Magnesium is a light, silvery-white, and relatively tough metal.
 
• It is not found as a free element in nature but occurs in combination with other elements like carbonates, sulfates, and silicates.
 
• Magnesium was isolated by Sir Humphry Davy in 1808.
 
 
 
• **Silver**
 
 
• Silver is a precious metal with high economic value.
 
• It is known for its high conductivity and luster.
 
• Silver has been used in jewelry, coins, and various industrial applications.
 
• It has been used by humans for thousands of years, but not as early as copper.
 
 
 
• **Gold**
 
 
• Gold is a highly valued precious metal known for its rarity and beauty.
 
• It has been used by humans for over 6,000 years.
 
• Gold is often associated with wealth and has been used in jewelry, currency, and as a standard for monetary systems.
 
 
 
• **Copper**
 
 
• Copper is a reddish-brown metal with high thermal and electrical conductivity.
 
• It was one of the first metals to be used by humans, primarily for tools and ornaments.
 
• Copper can be found as native copper or in minerals such as chalcopyrite and malachite.
 
• It played a crucial role in the development of early human civilizations.
